newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall St slipstream pulls Euroshares higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall St slipstream pulls Euroshares higher.

text.p: European shares were wafted higher on Friday by the second 80 point rise on Wall St in a row, but the buying in Europe was not as enthusiastic as on Thursday.
"It looks like the U.S. bull market isn't over just yet," the head of trading at a large brokerage in London said.
Elsewhere, the dollar slipped and gold retreated on worries that central banks could be selling bullion.

By midday, London's FTSE index of top shares had climbed 27.9 points, or 0.66 percent, to 4,256.3, while in Frankfurt the DAX index was up 11.17 points, or 0.37 percent, at 3,028.49. But France's CAC 40 index reversed a small early gain and was down 5.9 points, or 0.24 percent, at 2.497.16.
Wall Street's Dow Jones industrial average ended up 83.12 points at 6,823.86 overnight, extending Wednesday's gain of 85 points, which was its first gain after five days of losses.
Over the last two days the Dow has recouped two thirds of what it lost during its five-day skid.
The U.S. market was relieved that Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan did not provide any surprises in his testimony to the Senate Finance Committee about the economy on Thursday.
The Fed chief gave little hint that the central bank was considering raising interest rates at the February 4 and 5 meeting of the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee.
But strong U.S. gross domestic product data, due at 1330 GMT, could raise fears of a March rate hike economists said.
A Reuters poll of economists showed U.S. GDP for the fourth quarter of 1996 was expected to show growth of 3.9 percent after a rise of 2.1 percent previously.
Higher interest rates would sorely test the world's share markets, many of which are at or near record levels, by making returns on alternative investments and cash more attractive.
Meanwhile, dealers in London said that if the Dow remained steady, the FTSE could test its all-time highs of 4,273.4 set on January 23 over the next few sessions.
"Not everyone is convinced that the Dow will keep up the momentum," one dealer said. "But if we have another Dow spurt today, that should be enough to push the FTSE 100 over the top."
Germany's DAX index rose in early trade, nearing its all time high of 3041.55, though some of its gains then evaporated.
Software firm SAP rose 10 percent after posting stronger than expected 1996 earnings. Porsche also soared after first-half profits surged.
In France, Europe's most bullish market on Thursday, shares also rose, only to slip to a small loss as the market consolidated ahead of the expiry of the CAC futures.

In currencies, the dollar drifted lower against the mark and yen as the market took a lack of fresh incentives as a chance to adjust after the recent rally and ahead of the fourth quarter U.S. GDP data.
"People have been universally bullish on the dollar for some time, and when you ask around who's long and who's short, you don't find anyone's who's short," said a trader at a U.S. bank.

Traders said remarks by German and Japanese officials overnight expressing concerns about the currency market were weighing on the dollar. Support levels were broken on the way down, accelerating its fall against the mark and the yen. The dollar was at 1.6337 marks and 121.37 yen at midday.
The pound was vulnerable after heavy selling against the dollar and yen spilled over into mark trade too. By midday, the pound stood at around $1.60 and 2.6190 marks.
Gold fixed at $345.00, its lowest since September 14, 1993, after the price crumbled overnight, pulling platinum down also.
"It is not confirmed but everyone is saying that a central bank has been selling," a European-based bullion dealer said.
Gold, which has plunged from about $370 at the start of the year, has also been shunned by investors who prefer to pour money into the booming U.S. stock market.
Analysts say the market may find some buying around $341, with support at $330, the low of 1993.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6337 marks and 121.37 yen, compared with late Thursday's European levels of 1.6382 marks and 121.61 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was up 27.9 points at 4,256.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 5.90 points at 2,497.16.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 11.17 points at 3,028.49.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $345.00, its lowest since September 14, 1993, down sharply from Thursday's late fix of $349.25, and close at $347.35 in Europe on Thursday.
Platinum was also down sharply with gold, fixing at $350.25, its Lowest in 3-3/4 years and down $2.50 from Thursday.
